test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 06 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Let AB and CD be two parallel lines and PQ be a transversal such that PQ intersects AB at the point R and CD at the point S, respectively. If ∠BRP = (2x + 13)° and ∠DSP = (3x − 22)°, then find ∠CSP.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify that ∠BRP and ∠DSP are **corresponding angles**, which are equal for **parallel lines**.

Equate the expressions: 2x + 13 = 3x − 22 ⇒ x = 35.

Calculate ∠DSP = 3(35) − 22 = 83°.

Since ∠CSP and ∠DSP form a **linear pair** on line CD, their sum is 180°.

∠CSP = 180° − 83° = 97°.

**∴ The correct answer is 97°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Line **AB || CD** and **PQ** is a **transversal**.

∠BRP = (2x + 13)° and ∠DSP = (3x − 22)°.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Corresponding Angles:** When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, the corresponding angles are equal.

2. **Linear Pair:** The sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d53e407b085c167c5e358bf851c06d37a9b907ebbf1f240510f0007e1a953f2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since **AB || CD**, ∠BRP = ∠DSP (**Corresponding angles**)

⇒ 2x + 13 = 3x − 22

⇒ 13 + 22 = 3x − 2x

⇒ x = 35

⇒ Now, ∠DSP = 3(35) − 22

⇒ ∠DSP = 105 − 22 = 83°

⇒ On the straight line **CD**, ∠CSP + ∠DSP = 180° (**Linear pair**)

⇒ ∠CSP + 83° = 180°

⇒ ∠CSP = 180° − 83°

⇒ ∠CSP = 97°

**∴ The correct answer is 97°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines are equal (e.g., ∠ARS = ∠DSR).

Consecutive Interior Angles

Angles on the same side of the transversal and between the parallel lines are supplementary (sum = 180°).

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other at the vertex are always equal.</p
